mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.25% indicates aggressive monetary easing, compressing discount rates for equity valuation and generating positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS <= 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate (UNRATE > 8.5%) signals economic weakness triggering aggressive monetary policy, resulting in positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 8.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate consumer demand contraction, causing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline.

mechanism_narrative: A manufacturing output contraction (INDPRO < 90) indicates supply chain disruption reducing corporate profitability, generating negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO < 90.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth (GDPC1 > 3.0% annualized) indicates robust economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when GDPC1 > 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained inflation above 3.0% (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY) signals monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous payroll growth (PAYEMS) and unemployment decline (UNRATE) indicate labor market strength, generating positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases.

mechanism_narrative: Monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) reduce liquidity, causing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%.
